compiled_state.description:
# Config-driven type mapping + type-granular skip (collapse round-trip via rebar-type label)

## Context / Problem

Ticket-type mapping is hardcoded (`value_maps.LOCAL_TYPE_TO_JIRA`) and whole-type sync
exclusion is a fixed set (`config.EXCLUDED_SYNC_TYPES`). A Jira project that lacks a rebar
type (e.g. no `Story`) has no configured recourse today: it can't remap the type to an
analog (Epic→Initiative) and can't cleanly skip the missing type. Type must become
config-driven on the S1 core with three outcomes: **remap**, **skip** (type-granular
whole-ticket exclusion), and **fail-closed** on an unmapped-non-skipped type. Because
rebar may have more types than Jira, a **non-injective collapse** must be allowed and made
round-trip-safe via a new `rebar-type:` annotation label, symmetric with `rebar-status:`.

## Approach

Wire the S1 `type_map` axis. Outbound: resolve the effective type map over the built-in
default (`LOCAL_TYPE_TO_JIRA`); a mapped type is remapped; a type whose config value is
the sentinel `skip` extends the excluded-from-sync behavior (`EXCLUDED_SYNC_TYPES`) at
per-project granularity; an **unmapped, non-skipped** type is a **fail-closed load error**
(surfaced by S1 `validate`) — never a silent drift. When distinct rebar types collapse to
one Jira type, stamp a `rebar-type:<local>` label (new, mirroring the existing
`rebar-status:` label machinery in `inbound_fields.py`) so inbound recovers the original
rebar type. Inbound: prefer the `rebar-type:` label, else invert the effective map.
Document the hierarchy consequence: collapsing to a same/lower Jira hierarchy level
forfeits the parent role, so children fall to the S7 breadcrumb path.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/config.py` — type resolution + per-project skip.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_family/value_maps.py` — built-in
  default becomes injected fallback.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_fields.py` — `rebar-type:` label recovery.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_type_mapping.py` (new).

## Testing

- **Config-effect contrast (unit):** with `type_map.epic="Initiative"`, an outbound epic
  targets `Initiative`; default targets the built-in value — same path, different config.
- **Skip (per-project):** a type mapped to `skip` excludes that type's tickets from sync
  for that project only; another project still syncs it — asserted on the sync decision.
- **Fail-closed (failure path):** an unmapped non-skipped type raises the named validation
  error at load; the nearest valid config does not raise.
- **Round-trip (collapse):** collapsed types stamp `rebar-type:` labels; inbound recovers
  each distinct rebar type.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Effective type map = built-in ← `default` ← `projects.<KEY>`; a non-default overlay
  changes the outbound type through the real path — verified by
  `test_type_mapping.py::test_type_config_effect`.
- [ ] A `skip`-mapped type excludes that type from sync per-project only — verified by
  `test_type_mapping.py::test_type_skip_per_project`.
- [ ] An unmapped non-skipped type fails closed at load with a named error — verified by
  `test_type_mapping.py::test_unmapped_type_fails_closed`.
- [ ] Collapsed types round-trip losslessly via `rebar-type:` labels — verified by
  `test_type_mapping.py::test_type_collapse_roundtrip`.

Test tier: **in-process unit** — type resolution, skip decision, and label round-trip are
pure functions; oracles are the produced type field, the sync decision, the raised error,
and the recovered type.
